# Intake brief: Re-sync generated Vite config's watcher-ignore so main-checkout dev servers and test runs stop exhausting inotify (ENOSPC)

## Problem statement

Running the full test suite from the main checkout fails with repeated
`ENOSPC: System limit for number of file watchers reached` (17 vite-node CLI
test failures in the latest run) because the Vite/Vitest file watcher recursively
traverses `.worklog/worktrees/**` — 18 worktree checkouts totalling ~7 500 extra
files — exhausting the machine-wide `fs.inotify.max_user_watches` (65 536) under
concurrent processes. The repo's checked-in `vite.config.ts` predates (and never
received) the core scaffold template's watcher-ignore guard that fixes exactly
this failure mode, so the bug persists on every main-checkout dev server start
and test run.

## Users

- **Developers/agents maintaining main-street** — must be able to run the test
  suite and dev server from the main checkout without host-wide watcher limits
  being hit.
  - *User story:* "As a developer, I want `npm test` and `npm run dev` to work
    from the main checkout so I can verify changes and the audit skill's F3
    re-runs without tripping a host inotify limit."
- **Audit/verification tooling** — the post-push belt-and-suspenders validation
  and the audit skill's cache-miss auto-execution depend on a green main-checkout
  suite.
  - *User story:* "As the verification pipeline, I want the full suite to pass
    from the main checkout so finished work can be independently confirmed."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `vite.config.ts` wires the shared ignore list into the Vite file watcher:
   it imports `DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS` from `./core/scripts/vite-transcript-plugin`
   and sets `server.watch.ignored: [...DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS]`, and that list
   contains `**/.worklog/**` — verified by a unit regression test that mirrors the
   core `game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` ENOSPC guard and asserts the real config file.
2. Starting the Vite dev server (and the Vitest projects) from the main checkout
   registers **no** watchers under `.worklog/**` — asserted deterministically via
   `server.watcher.getWatched()` keys (or equivalent), ported from the core
   `vite-transcript-plugin-regression.test.ts` AC3/AC4 pattern.
3. A full test-suite run from the **main checkout** (via the test skill) completes
   with no ENOSPC watcher failures — the 17 previously failing vite-node CLI tests
   pass.
4. No regression to existing behaviour: the `unit` / `unit-cli` project split
   (MS-0MV5PNIPO00940KG), dev-output watch handling (`data`, `tmp`, `results`,
   `dist`), and `resolvePagesBase`/`cardResultsWriterPlugin` remain intact.
5. Related documentation updated to reflect the ENOSPC guard and the
   `.worklog/**` watch exclusion (config comment matching the template wording;
   README/dev-notes as applicable). CHANGELOG.md excluded — managed by the ship
   skill's release pipeline.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- `vite.config.ts` is declared AUTO-GENERATED by `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`,
  and the current template (core submodule pinned at `dc4ec0ce`) **already** emits
  the watcher guard — do **not** modify the core template or any `core/` file.
- **Do not blind re-scaffold** (`npm run scaffold`): the current template lacks this
  repo's local `unit-cli` project isolation (MS-0MV5PNIPO00940KG), `CLI_TEST_FILES`,
  `cardResultsWriterPlugin`, and `resolvePagesBase` additions; a blind re-scaffold
  would regress them. Apply a surgical sync of the `server.watch.ignored` block only.
- Host-level tuning (raising `fs.inotify.max_user_watches`) is **out of scope** —
  it is privileged and masks the root cause; the fix must require no kernel changes.
- Stale-worktree pruning (4+ worktrees for completed items — MS-0MUXAL8HC005P9E4,
  MS-0MUYFXBC4003073C, MS-0MV2DPSVB004B1WX, `f7-competitive-before-85d23dbb`) is an
  operational prerequisite for a clean main-checkout validation run, gated on
  operator approval for others' worktrees (cleanup skill) — not part of this code
  change.
- Test-execution policy: all agent-initiated test runs go through the test skill.

## Existing state

- `vite.config.ts` `server:` block has `port`/`open` only — no `watch.ignored` —
  so the watcher walks `.worklog/worktrees/**` (18 worktrees, ~7 457 files / 624
  dirs outside `node_modules`, measured) and exhausts inotify under concurrent
  runs. Measured machine-wide watch usage 18 535 / 65 536 at idle — headroom is
  intermittent, not guaranteed.
- The core scaffold template already contains the guard and core regression tests
  assert it (CG-0MV5SEHHG000ZKUA completed, CG-0MTJ7A4Z3000MFMV); `tce-the-rising`
  has the generated block, main-street never received the re-sync.
- Failure evidence: post-push main-checkout suite reruns fail only with ENOSPC
  referencing stale worktree paths; the worktree finish-gate full suite passes green.

## Desired change

- Import `DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS` from `./core/scripts/vite-transcript-plugin`
  and add `watch: { ignored: [...DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS] }` to the existing
  `server:` block, with a short comment explaining the `.worklog/worktrees` ENOSPC
  guard (matching the template/tce-the-rising wording). All local project fixtures
  (`unit`, `unit-cli`, `browser`) stay untouched.
- Add a unit regression test asserting the real config wires the ignore list and
  that `.worklog/**` is covered (e.g. `tests/deploy/vite-watch-ignore-enospc.test.ts`,
  alongside the existing `tests/deploy/vite-*` config tests).

## Key Files:

- `vite.config.ts` — add `DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS` import + `server.watch.ignored`; document the guard
- `tests/deploy/vite-watch-ignore-enospc.test.ts` (new) — regression: config wires ignore list; `.worklog/**` covered; no `.worklog` paths in `server.watcher.getWatched()` (pattern with `tests/deploy/preview-smoke.test.ts` / core's `vite-transcript-plugin-regression.test.ts`)
- `README.md` / dev docs — note the `.worklog/**` watch exclusion and main-checkout run guidance, as applicable

## Related work

- MS-0MVA50KJN009X30C — [test-failure] `<suite exited 1>`: `npm --silent test` (completed; same root suite-exit failure mode)
- MS-0MUZH51PU007POJ4 — Colour card faces by synergy type (completed; the item whose finish exposed the ENOSPC recurrence)
- MS-0MV5PNIPO00940KG — [test-failure] Main Street vite-node CLI tests flake under vitest file-level parallelism (completed; the `unit-cli` project isolation that a blind re-scaffold would regress)
- CG-0MV5SEHHG000ZKUA — core: `game-repo-scaffold` renderViteConfig omits `server.watch.ignored` (completed; template-side fix — this item ports it into main-street's checked-in config)
- CG-0MTJ7A4Z3000MFMV / CG-0MTJ560IZ005XAZC — core: vite-transcript-plugin ENOSPC hardening and deviation items (completed)
- **Discovered:** the same missing `server.watch.ignored` block exists in 8 sibling game repos (AI_Hell, tce-beleaguered-castle, tce-blackjack, tce-coloretto, tce-feudalism, tce-golf, tce-lost-cities, tce-sushi-go) — tracked as a separate derived work item, out of scope here.

## Assumptions & risks

- **Assumption:** the durable, testable deliverable is the checked-in config sync;
  worktree pruning and host tuning are operational/privileged and outside the repo
  change (recorded in the brief, not the ACs). (OPEN QUESTION if the operator wants
  them in scope after all.)
- **Risk (low):** chokidar ignore-glob semantics — `**/.worklog/**` matches the
  `.worklog/worktrees/**` tree; validated by the core regression suite and the
  deterministic watcher assertion in AC2. Mitigation: port the same assertion
  pattern used in core tests.
- **Risk (medium):** config-test flakiness from real dev-server startup under
  parallelism — mitigation: keep the watcher-population assertion best-effort/deterministic
  like the core regression test (AC2), and rely on AC3's full-suite run for the
  end-to-end guarantee.
- **Risk (scope creep):** sibling-repo porting, worktree pruning, and host tuning
  are tempting adds — recorded as related work items/notes, not this item's scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- No interactive clarifying questions were required: the item's description
  (with the operator-approved remediation list) plus repo evidence fully resolved
  the problem, root cause, and intended fix.
- Research summary: root cause isolated to the missing `server.watch.ignored`
  guard in the checked-in `vite.config.ts` (the core scaffold template at submodule
  `dc4ec0ce` already emits it; core tests CG-0MV5SEHHG000ZKUA guard it; the
  generated file predates the change). Evidence: `vite.config.ts` (no watch block),
  `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` (template has it), `core/tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts`
  (assertion), `.worklog/worktrees/` (18 stale checkouts), inotify usage measurement.
- Decision: issue type corrected `chore` → `bug` (current behaviour is broken —
  dev server and test runs crash with ENOSPC); priority stays `medium`
  (infra/verification friction, not a blocked pipeline). Host tuning and pruning
  recorded as out-of-scope/related (see above).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MUQZH5PH001JXLV** – Core scaffold template Pages base (completed)
- **MS-0MVBEQ6MC004WRI0** – Port Vite watcher-ignore (server.watch.ignored) to sibling game repos' generated vite.config.ts (open)
- **MS-0MUSY1K6B00095AT** – Storyline editor test harness & fixtures (open)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: able, ac4, acceptance, add, adds (+295 more)
- `core/AGENTS.md` — matched: able, acceptance, add, adds, agent (+232 more)
- `core/CHANGELOG.md` — matched: 0mv5sehhg000zkua, able, ac2, add, adds (+185 more)

# Intake Brief: Add ToneForge factories for the four intentionally factory-less SFX mappings

## Problem statement

The Main Street runtime synth currently ships 12 ToneForge factories, but 16 logical SFX keys are mapped — four keys intentionally fall back to WAV because no ToneForge factory exists for them. This work item adds real ToneForge synth factories for those four keys so the synth covers all 16 mapped keys, then removes the factory-less workaround entries.

## Users

- **Game player** — expects consistent synthetic audio for all Main Street SFX rather than a mix of synth and WAV sounds.
- **Developer** — the tutorial and gameplay emit zero `[tfAdapter] Missing tf factory` warnings for Main Street, keeping the console clean.

Example user stories:
- As a player, I want all Main Street SFX to use the ToneForge synth consistently, so the audio experience is unified.
- As a developer, I want no missing-factory warnings on the console when playing Main Street, so real issues stand out.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **All four new factories exist in the runtime synth module** — `income-positive-chime`, `income-negative-chime`, `income-neutral-chime`, and `success-fanfare` are present in `main-street-runtime-synth.mjs` (`factories` and `descriptors`), each producing a musically appropriate one-shot sound.
2. **All 16 mapped SFX keys play through the synth** — every key in `MAIN_STREET_TF_SFX_MAPPING` is handled by the synth player (no WAV fallback), verified by `tests/main-street/tfFallback.test.ts` (no factory-less assertion for these keys).
3. **Factory-less workaround lists are updated** — `MAIN_STREET_TF_FACTORYLESS_KEYS` and `MAIN_STREET_TF_FACTORYLESS_FACTORY_KEYS` in `src/sfx-tf-mapping.ts` no longer contain the four keys (the arrays become empty).
4. **Logger and tests stay consistent** — `src/tf/tfLogger.ts` `EXPECTED_FACTORYLESS_KEYS` no longer references these four keys; `tests/main-street/tutorial-console-cleanliness.test.ts` no longer asserts WAV fallback for the four keys (or asserts they play through synth instead).
5. **Full test suite passes** — all existing tests pass, including `tfFallback.test.ts` and `tutorial-console-cleanliness.test.ts`.

## Constraints

- New factories must follow the existing pattern in `main-street-runtime-synth.mjs` (one-shot voice, Tone synthesizer, appropriate musical character).
- Preserve the existing 12 factories unchanged.
- The four new sounds should be musically appropriate:
  - `income-positive-chime`: pleasant ascending chime (positive reinforcement)
  - `income-negative-chime`: descending/flat tone (negative feedback, not alarming)
  - `income-neutral-chime`: single soft note (neutral indication)
  - `success-fanfare`: short celebratory multi-note fanfare
- No changes to the engine/core beyond the runtime synth module.
- No new external dependencies.

## Existing state

- `core/src/core-engine/tf-runtime/main-street-runtime-synth.mjs` — ships 12 factories with `descriptors` and `factories` exports; uses helper functions `oneShotVoice()`, `movementVoice()`, `ambienceVoice()`, etc.
- `src/sfx-tf-mapping.ts` — maps 16 keys; 4 intentionally factory-less (tracked in `MAIN_STREET_TF_FACTORYLESS_KEYS`).
- `src/tf/tfLogger.ts` — suppresses missing-factory warnings for the 4 factory-less keys.
- `tests/main-street/tfFallback.test.ts` — asserts that factory-less keys fall back to WAV.
- `tests/main-street/tutorial-console-cleanliness.test.ts` — asserts no console warnings for the factory-less keys.

## Key Files

- `core/src/core-engine/tf-runtime/main-street-runtime-synth.mjs` — Add 4 new factory entries and descriptor entries.
- `src/sfx-tf-mapping.ts` — Remove 4 keys from `MAIN_STREET_TF_FACTORYLESS_KEYS`.
- `src/tf/tfLogger.ts` — No code change needed (it derives `EXPECTED_FACTORYLESS_KEYS` from the mapping dynamically), but verify.
- `tests/main-street/tfFallback.test.ts` — Remove/assertion update for the four keys (they should now play via synth).
- `tests/main-street/tutorial-console-cleanliness.test.ts` — Update any assertions that expect WAV fallback for the four keys.

## Related work

- **MS-0MUU9QYQE006NLEZ** — Activate ToneForge runtime synth: loader diagnostics + scene wiring (completed)
- **MS-0MV26MOWT004ZCQC** — Console noise when running the tutorial (completed) — silenced per-play warnings for factory-less keys
- **CG-0MUU9PSWC009CW76** — Engine contract: WAV fallback for missing factories
- **CG-0MUTU0MFE0077H0F** — Engine ToneForge foundation

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the four sounds should be synthesized (not WAV) — consistent with the synth-first approach of the runtime module.
- **Assumption:** each sound is a short one-shot (≤ 1 second) — consistent with the existing factory pattern.
- **Risk:** musical quality of synthesized sounds is subjective. Mitigation: keep sounds simple and consistent with the existing 12 factories.
- **Risk:** the runtime synth module is a static ESM file that gets bundled — adding factories should not change bundle size meaningfully.
- **Scope-creep:** adding more factory-less keys from other games is out of scope; this item covers only the four Main Street keys.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interactive interview round was required: the seed context plus extensive repository evidence determined scope and approach.

- Q: "What musical character should each of the four sounds have?" — Answer (inferred from names): positive-chime (pleasant ascending), negative-chime (descending/flat but not alarming), neutral-chime (soft single note), success-fanfare (celebratory multi-note). Source: work-item title + naming convention.
- Q: "Should the logger file be updated manually?" — Answer: no manual change needed — `tfLogger.ts` derives `EXPECTED_FACTORYLESS_KEYS` dynamically from `sfx-tf-mapping.ts`, so removing from the mapping list automatically removes them from the logger's suppression set. Source: repo evidence, `src/tf/tfLogger.ts` lines 35-42.
